youtube.title: The Dust Tail Hubble Just Photographed
youtube.description:
Hubble new discovery: a tail of dark, fluffy dust 63 light-years away, photographed in visible light for the first time.

Reported 11-13 November 2026 from a study in The Astrophysical Journal Letters. Around the young star Beta Pictoris, Webb found a tail in infrared in 2024. Hubble looked six times between 2012 and 2025 and now shows it in visible light. In this 2-minute explainer you will learn what the tail is made of, how long earlier estimates said it could be (up to about 93 billion miles), the collision idea behind it, and what scientists say is still uncertain.

00:00 A tail around a star
00:20 Webb saw it first
00:37 Six looks
01:03 Fluffy and dark
01:19 What we do not know

Question for the comments: what should Hubble and Webb look at next?

Sources (read 18 Nov 2026):
- ThePrint, 11 Nov 2026: https://theprint.in/feature/a-collision-between-pluto-sized-bodies-study-investigates-a-mysterious-dust-cloud-spotted-by-nasa/3095822/
- Nature World News, 13 Nov 2026: https://www.natureworldnews.com/articles/73857/20261113/fluffy-carbon-dust-63-light-years-away-shows-what-our-young-solar-system-may-have-looked-like.htm
- The Astrophysical Journal Letters, DOI 10.3847/2041-8213/aeac4a
If a figure here is out of date, the sources above are the reference.

Voice and visuals in this video are AI-generated. Characters and events are fictional. (The news facts come from the sources above; Mia, the stargazer, is an invented character.)
Music: original score made for this channel.
